sourceLesson: Backend LLD: OOP-4: ABCs, Protocols and Mixins

questions.title: Abstract Method Instantiation Guarantee
questions.question: What does @abstractmethod on a method inside an ABC subclass guarantee?

options.optionText: The method runs automatically when the object is created
Any subclass that does not implement this method cannot be instantiated — TypeError at object creation
The method is private and inaccessible from outside
The method is optimized for performance

questions.title: Inherited Abstract Method Satisfaction
questions.question: A PaymentGateway ABC has two abstract methods. StripeGateway inherits from it and implements both. StripeGateway is then subclassed by StripeGatewayV2 which adds a new method but does NOT re-implement the abstract ones. Can StripeGatewayV2() be instantiated?

options.optionText: No — each subclass must re-implement all abstract methods
Only if StripeGatewayV2 explicitly calls super()
Only if StripeGatewayV2 also inherits from ABC
Yes — StripeGateway already satisfied the contract, and StripeGatewayV2 inherits those implementations

questions.title: Protocol Runtime Check Requirement
questions.question: A Protocol is defined without @runtime_checkable. What happens when you call isinstance(some_obj, MyProtocol)?

options.optionText: Returns True if methods match
Returns False always
TypeError — isinstance requires @runtime_checkable to work with Protocols
Works normally — @runtime_checkable is only for static checkers

questions.title: Purpose Of Mixin Classes
questions.question: A mixin named TimestampMixin adds a created_at attribute. It is designed to be combined via multiple inheritance. Which statement is true about mixins, per the lecture?

options.optionText: Mixins represent an "is-a" relationship
Mixins should be instantiated directly and used standalone
Mixins must inherit from ABC
Mixins add focused, reusable capabilities — never meant to be instantiated alone, combined via multiple inheritance
Every time an instance of the class is created (__init__ equivalent for classes)
Automatically when a new subclass is defined — at class-definition time, not at instance-creation time
Only when explicitly called with super().__init_subclass__()
Only in metaclasses

questions.title: Multiple Parent Method Priority
questions.question: class RGW(PaymentGateway, LoggingMixin, JSONMixin) — all three parents define describe(). Whose version does RGW().describe() call?

options.optionText: LoggingMixin's — mixins override everything
JSONMixin's — last parent wins
PaymentGateway's — it appears first in the MRO after RGW itself
All three run in sequence

questions.title: Class Type Hierarchy
questions.question: The type() of an ordinary Python class (e.g., type(str)) is:

options.optionText: object
type
ABCMeta
classmethod

questions.title: Abstract Method Name-Only Check
questions.question: An ABC defines @abstractmethod def validate(self). A subclass implements validate but with a different signature (def validate(self, strict=False)). Can the subclass be instantiated?

options.optionText: Yes — Python only checks that a method with the name validate exists on the subclass, not its exact signature
No — signatures must match exactly
Only if strict has a default value
Raises TypeError at class definition

questions.title: Nominal Vs Structural Typing Distinction
questions.question: Which is the key difference between nominal typing (ABC) and structural typing (Protocol)?

options.optionText: Nominal checks method presence; structural checks inheritance
They are the same mechanism with different names
Structural typing does not support isinstance
Nominal requires the class to explicitly declare lineage via inheritance; structural only checks whether the required methods exist on the object

questions.title: Optional Keyword Registration Guard
questions.question: PaymentGateway uses __init_subclass__ with gateway_name keyword. A developer writes class TestGateway(PaymentGateway) (no gateway_name). Which is true?

options.optionText: TypeError — missing required keyword
__init_subclass__ still runs, but the if gateway_name: guard means the class is NOT added to registry — it exists as a normal subclass
__init_subclass__ does not run at all
registry stores it under the key None

questions.title: Abstract Method Enforcement Check
questions.question: Uber's checkout team builds a PaymentGateway ABC with @abstractmethod for process_payment and refund. A new developer writes class StripeGateway(PaymentGateway) implementing only process_payment, forgetting refund. They then write s = StripeGateway(). What happens?

options.optionText: Object is created, AttributeError only when s.refund() is called later
SyntaxError at class definition time
TypeError at instantiation — Python refuses to create an object of a class that hasn't implemented all abstract methods
Object is created with refund returning None by default

questions.title: Nominal Vs Structural Typing
questions.question: Uber integrates a third-party VendorFraudScanner (installed via pip, not editable) that has a scan(amount, location) method. The team defines class FraudChecker(ABC) with @abstractmethod def scan(...). What does isinstance(VendorFraudScanner(), FraudChecker) return, and why?

options.optionText: True — ABC checks method presence structurally
False — ABC uses nominal typing; the vendor class never inherited from FraudChecker, so it fails regardless of having the right methods
True — all classes satisfy any ABC by default
Raises TypeError

questions.title: Protocol Structural Type Check
questions.question: The team rewrites the fraud contract as @runtime_checkable class FraudCheckable(Protocol) with def scan(self, amount, location) -> bool. Without touching the vendor's code, what does isinstance(VendorFraudScanner(), FraudCheckable) now return?

options.optionText: False — Protocol also requires explicit inheritance
True — Protocol uses structural typing; it checks whether the object has a matching scan method, regardless of inheritance
Raises NotImplementedError
True only if @runtime_checkable is removed

questions.title: Multiple Mixin Method Resolution
questions.question: RazorpayGateway is declared as class RazorpayGateway(PaymentGateway, LoggingMixin, JSONSerializableMixin). Both PaymentGateway and LoggingMixin define a method called describe(). When razorpay.describe() is called, whose version runs?

options.optionText: PaymentGateway's — it comes before LoggingMixin in the MRO because it was listed first in the class declaration
LoggingMixin's — mixins always take priority
Python raises AmbiguityError
Both run sequentially

questions.title: Silent Registry Skip Behavior
questions.question: PaymentGateway uses __init_subclass__ with a gateway_name keyword to auto-register subclasses into PaymentGateway.registry. A new developer adds PaytmGateway but forgets gateway_name=... in the class declaration. What happens?

options.optionText: TypeError — gateway_name is required
registry auto-generates a name from the class name
__init_subclass__ doesn't run at all
The class is created normally, but it is NOT added to registry (the if gateway_name: guard skips it silently)
